title: The Creation
summary: God creates in six days by speaking: light, sky, land and seas, plants, sun, moon and stars, sea creatures and birds, land animals, and last humans, made male and female in God's image and given rule over the creatures. God calls the work good, rests on the seventh day and blesses it. Readers differ on whether the days are literal, figurative or literary, and on how this account relates to the second one in Genesis 2.

title: The Fall of Man
summary: The serpent asks the woman whether God forbade every tree, and she repeats the command with an addition about not touching the fruit. The serpent denies that she will die; she eats and gives some to her husband. They hide, God questions them, and each shifts blame. God announces pain, toil and death, clothes them, and sends them from Eden, posting cherubim and a flaming sword to guard the tree of life.

title: Cain and Abel
summary: Cain farms and Abel keeps sheep. God accepts Abel's offering but not Cain's, and warns the angry Cain that sin is crouching at the door. Cain speaks with Abel in the field and kills him, then answers God's question with 'Am I my brother's keeper?' God says Abel's blood cries from the ground, makes Cain a wanderer, and sets a mark on him so that no one will kill him. Cain settles east of Eden in Nod.

title: The Line of Seth
summary: After Abel's death Eve bears Seth, and in Seth's line people begin to call on the name of the LORD. The genealogy runs from Adam through ten generations to Noah, giving each man's age at the birth of his heir and at death. Enoch walks with God and is taken rather than dying; Methuselah lives longest, 969 years. Noah's father hopes he will bring relief from the cursed ground, and Noah fathers Shem, Ham and Japheth.

title: Noah and the Flood
summary: Noah, righteous in a violent world, is told to build an ark. He brings in his family and pairs of animals, and rain and the deep flood the earth until everything outside the ark dies. The ark rests on the mountains of Ararat, and Noah sends out a raven and a dove. He offers sacrifice after leaving the ark, and God promises never again to flood the whole earth, setting the rainbow as the sign of the covenant.

title: The Family of Noah
summary: Noah plants a vineyard, becomes drunk and lies uncovered. Ham sees him, while Shem and Japheth cover him, and Noah curses Ham's son Canaan and blesses Shem and Japheth. Genesis 10 then lists the descendants of Japheth, Ham and Shem by peoples, lands and languages, including Nimrod, a mighty hunter whose kingdom begins at Babel. Readers have long debated why the curse falls on Canaan rather than Ham.

title: The Tower of Babel
summary: Everyone shares one language and settles on a plain in Shinar. They resolve to build a city and a tower with its top in the heavens so that they can make a name for themselves and not be scattered. The LORD comes down to see the city, confuses their speech so that they cannot understand one another, and scatters them over the earth. The city is called Babel, a name the text connects with 'confused'.

title: The Call of Abram
summary: Terah's family leaves Ur of the Chaldees for Canaan but settles in Haran, where Terah dies. The LORD tells Abram to leave his country and father's house for a land he will be shown, promising to make him a great nation and to bless all families of the earth through him. At seventy-five Abram goes with Sarai, Lot and their households, building altars at Shechem and near Bethel and moving on toward the Negev.

title: Abram and Lot
summary: Quarreling herdsmen lead Abram to offer Lot his choice of land, and Lot picks the well-watered Jordan plain near Sodom. When four eastern kings defeat Sodom and carry off Lot, Abram arms 318 men, pursues the kings north to Dan, and recovers the captives and goods. Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, blesses Abram, who gives him a tenth. Abram refuses the king of Sodom's offer of the spoils.

title: Hagar and Ishmael
summary: Sarai, childless after years in Canaan, gives her Egyptian servant Hagar to Abram. When Hagar conceives and looks down on Sarai, Sarai treats her harshly and she flees into the wilderness. The angel of the LORD finds her by a spring, tells her to return, and promises numerous descendants and a son named Ishmael, 'God hears.' Hagar names God 'the God who sees me', goes back, and bears Ishmael when Abram is eighty-six.

title: Abraham and Sarah’s Covenant
summary: God appears when Abram is ninety-nine, renames him Abraham and Sarai Sarah, promises a son through Sarah and a covenant with Isaac, and commands circumcision of every male in the household as its sign. Abraham laughs at the promise. Soon after, three visitors accept his hospitality by the oaks of Mamre and repeat it; Sarah overhears and laughs, and is asked, 'Is any thing too hard for the LORD?'

title: Lot Leaves Sodom
summary: Two angels reach Sodom, and Lot shelters them. The men of the city demand the visitors, and Lot offers his daughters instead until the angels strike the crowd blind. They hurry Lot, his wife and two daughters out before fire and brimstone fall on Sodom and Gomorrah. Lot's wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt. In a cave, Lot's daughters, fearing they will have no children, get him drunk and bear Moab and Ben-ammi.

title: Isaac and Ishmael
summary: Sarah bears Isaac when Abraham is a hundred, and he is circumcised on the eighth day. At the feast for Isaac's weaning, Sarah sees Ishmael mocking and demands that Hagar and her son be sent away. Abraham is troubled, but God tells him to listen to Sarah and promises to make a nation of Ishmael too. In the wilderness of Beer-sheba the water runs out; God hears the boy, opens Hagar's eyes to a well, and Ishmael grows up an archer in Paran.

title: The Binding of Isaac
summary: God tests Abraham by telling him to offer Isaac, the son he loves, on a mountain in the land of Moriah. Abraham sets out with Isaac and two servants; Isaac asks where the lamb is, and Abraham answers that God will provide. As Abraham raises the knife, the angel of the LORD calls from heaven and stops him. Abraham finds a ram caught in a thicket and offers it, and the promise of blessing and countless descendants is renewed.

title: Isaac and Rebekah
summary: Abraham sends his oldest servant to his relatives in Mesopotamia to find a wife for Isaac and not from the Canaanites. At the well outside Nahor's city, the servant prays for a sign, and Rebekah, who offers water for him and his camels, proves to be Abraham's kin. Her brother Laban and her father Bethuel agree, and she consents to go at once. Isaac meets her in the field at evening, takes her into his mother's tent, and loves her.

title: Jacob and Esau
summary: Rebekah, long barren, bears twins after the LORD tells her the older will serve the younger. Esau sells his birthright to Jacob for stew. During a famine Isaac stays in Gerar, passes Rebekah off as his sister, and digs wells that herdsmen dispute. When he is old and blind, Rebekah helps Jacob disguise himself and take Esau's blessing. Esau vows to kill Jacob, so Isaac sends Jacob to Paddan-aram to find a wife, and Esau marries a daughter of Ishmael.

title: Jacob’s Household
summary: Jacob reaches Haran, meets Rachel at a well, and works seven years to marry her. Laban gives him Leah instead and then Rachel a week later for seven more years of work. Leah bears Reuben, Simeon, Levi and Judah; Rachel, barren, gives her servant Bilhah to Jacob, and Leah gives Zilpah. The sisters compete over children and mandrakes, and at last Rachel bears Joseph.

title: Jacob Returns to Canaan
summary: After twenty years Jacob leaves Laban secretly with his wives, children and flocks; Rachel takes her father's household gods. Laban overtakes him, and after a search the two make a covenant. Afraid of Esau, Jacob sends gifts ahead, then wrestles a man through the night at the Jabbok, is hurt in the hip, and is renamed Israel. Esau runs to embrace him, and Jacob settles near Shechem and builds an altar.

title: Dinah at Shechem
summary: Shechem, son of Hamor the Hivite, takes Dinah and then wants to marry her. Hamor proposes intermarriage, and Jacob's sons demand that all the men of the city be circumcised first. While the men are in pain on the third day, Simeon and Levi kill them, and the other brothers plunder the city. Jacob says they have made him odious to the land; they answer, 'Should he deal with our sister as with an harlot?'

title: The Death of Rachel
summary: God tells Jacob to go to Bethel, and he has his household put away foreign gods, which he buries under an oak. God renews the name Israel and the promise of the land. Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin near Ephrath, and Jacob sets up a pillar on her grave. Reuben lies with Bilhah, and the twelve sons are listed. Isaac dies at 180, and Esau and Jacob bury him.

title: Joseph and His Brothers
summary: Jacob favors Joseph with a long coat, and Joseph's reports and dreams of sheaves and stars bowing to him anger his brothers. Sent to check on them near Dothan, Joseph is thrown into a pit; at Judah's suggestion he is sold to traders for twenty pieces of silver. The brothers dip his coat in goat's blood and show it to Jacob, who mourns. Joseph is sold in Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh.

title: Judah and Tamar
summary: Judah's eldest son Er dies, then Onan, who refuses to give Tamar a child in his brother's name. Judah withholds his youngest son Shelah. Tamar disguises herself as a veiled prostitute, takes Judah's signet, cord and staff as a pledge, and conceives. When she is condemned for her pregnancy, she produces the items, and Judah says, 'She hath been more righteous than I.' She bears twins, Perez and Zerah.

title: Joseph in Egypt
summary: Sold to Potiphar, Joseph prospers until Potiphar's wife accuses him falsely and he is jailed. In prison he interprets the dreams of Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker, but the cupbearer forgets him for two years. When Pharaoh dreams of fat and lean cattle and grain, Joseph interprets seven years of plenty followed by seven of famine and advises storing grain. Pharaoh makes him second in command, and Joseph marries Asenath, who bears Manasseh and Ephraim.

title: Joseph Reunites His Family
summary: Famine sends Jacob's sons to Egypt, where Joseph recognizes them but is not recognized; he accuses them of spying and keeps Simeon until they bring Benjamin. On a second trip Joseph's silver cup is placed in Benjamin's sack, and Judah offers himself in Benjamin's place. Joseph weeps and reveals himself, saying God sent him ahead to preserve life. Pharaoh invites the family, and Jacob, 130, comes to Egypt and is settled in Goshen.

title: Jacob Blesses His Family
summary: Jacob adopts Joseph's sons Ephraim and Manasseh, blessing the younger first. He then speaks over his twelve sons, including Judah, to whom the scepter will not depart, and tells them to bury him at Machpelah. After his death and burial in Canaan, the brothers fear Joseph will repay them, and he answers that God meant it for good. Joseph dies at 110, asking that his bones be carried out of Egypt.
